### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**4** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4957ee5ef0e660fc9ee4525d83f13aa32ef8e969` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `fa02d5f3ab4b27c4d6803d99756680f5cea0c222` — the merge of head `25ba591849c1aaad8956e0dd21423189c7aed620` into base `4957ee5ef0e660fc9ee4525d83f13aa32ef8e969`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin fa02d5f3ab4b27c4d6803d99756680f5cea0c222 && git checkout fa02d5f3ab4b27c4d6803d99756680f5cea0c222
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4957ee5ef0e660fc9ee4525d83f13aa32ef8e969 25ba591849c1aaad8956e0dd21423189c7aed620 && git checkout -B drift-repro 4957ee5ef0e660fc9ee4525d83f13aa32ef8e969 && git merge --no-ff 25ba591849c1aaad8956e0dd21423189c7aed620

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4957ee5ef0e660fc9ee4525d83f13aa32ef8e969
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `25ba591849c1aaad8956e0dd21423189c7aed620`
Local-runs: none

Inputs, and nothing else: card #20867 (its body and all four comments: triage `5912878801`, claim `5921235126`, os-dev-report `5921673071`, ACCEPT `5921695101`); PR #20971 (its body, its file list, the net diff of the head against the merge-base `f6ccca4a44` with `origin/main`); the check-runs on the head, latest run per name. The dispatching seat's conclusions were read as claims to test, never as inputs. Read-only: nothing built, run, re-run or ablated; every source line cited below was read out of git objects at the head and at the merge-base.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Public surface: nothing moves — right.** `@objectstack/service-analytics` is published (`private` unset, `files` ships `dist`), its `exports` map is `.` only, and `src/index.ts` at the head re-exports from `dimension-labels.ts` only `resolveDimensionLabels`, `pickDisplayField`, `createOrderLabelResolver`, `withLabelFetchCache` and the types `DimensionLabelDeps`, `FieldMetaLite`, `OrderLabelResolver`; nothing from `preview-evaluator.ts`. `formatDateBucket` and `bucketDate` are reachable only inside the package (a tree-wide grep at the head finds no importer outside `packages/services/service-analytics`; the hits are ADR and design prose and CHANGELOG history). No published symbol is added, removed or retyped.
2. **`formatDateBucket`: a string key is recognised by core's reader and returned as written — right.** The recogniser is `bucketKeyToCalendarRange(value, granularity) !== null`, core's one reader of the keys `bucketDateKey` writes; it answers `null` for an unpadded `50-06` or `49-W52`, so nothing is relabelled that the writer did not write (triage's first bullet). For a key in 1000..9999 the output is byte-identical to the base: the removed year branch answered `String(y)` for the same string, a quarter, month or day key round-tripped through the parse to its own spelling, and an ISO week label failed the parse and was returned unchanged. For 0001..0999, `0050`, `0050-06`, `0050-06-15` now label as written where the base answered `1970` (pure digits read as epoch seconds), `50-06`, `50-06-15`. The signature `(value: unknown, granularity?: DateGranularity | string): unknown` is unchanged and every non-key still falls through to the parse path, so no input is refused.
3. **`formatDateBucket`: the raw-value relabel is `bucketDateKey(d, labelGranularity)` in UTC — right.** For 1000..9999 the bytes equal the removed local spelling (`bucketKeyYear` is a four-wide `padStart`, a no-op at four digits; the month and day padding is the same two-wide pad). Below 1000 the year is four digits. `week`, an unstated and an off-vocabulary granularity still label a raw value as its own `day` key (`labelGranularity` falls to `'day'`), as before. No timezone is passed, so the module's UTC-only contract (ADR-0053 D2's seam note: this is a re-labeller of already-bucketed values) is kept — no accepted ADR is reversed.
4. **The numeric year branch (`y` in 1000..9999 → `String(y)`) is kept as-is — right, and flagged.** A numeric `50` under `year` still reads as epoch ms and labels `1970`. Judged in ③ (F1).
5. **`bucketDate` is one call, `bucketDateKey(value, granularity, timezone)` — right.** Triage's second bullet, met literally: no second padding, no second week rule. Runtime deltas, for every year: (i) the `week` key is the ISO label `YYYY-Www`, no longer the Monday's `YYYY-MM-DD`; (ii) a finite number is bucketed as epoch ms (the base answered `null`, the empty bucket); (iii) a `Date` is read directly (the base re-parsed `String(date)`, which lands a year below 100 in the 1900s). Below 1000 the year is four digits. The timezone rule is the same helper the removed code called (`calendarPartsInTzOrUtc`, now inside the writer): unset, `'UTC'` or invalid keeps UTC. Each delta lands the preview on the published path's own answer: `@objectstack/objectql`'s `bucketDateValue`, the in-memory grouping's bucketer, is `bucketDateKey(value, granularity, timezone)` at the head (`packages/objectql/src/in-memory-aggregation.ts`), and the drivers' bucket SQL is what that writer's docblock binds its labels to.
6. **The parameter narrowing `string` → `BucketGranularity` is not an accept-set narrowing — right.** The one production caller, `evaluateAnalyticsQueryOverRows`, feeds `bucketDate` from `granByDim` (the query's `timeDimensions[].granularity`, typed `TimeUpdateInterval`) or from `dim.granularities[0]` (the same enum); `TimeUpdateInterval` is `z.enum(DateGranularity.options)` and `DateGranularity` is `['day', 'week', 'month', 'quarter', 'year']` (`packages/spec/src/data/query.zod.ts`); the dataset door's `dateGranularity` is `DateGranularity`. So every value a door admits is one of the five, `hour` is refused at the enum before either reader runs, and the removed `String(...)` at the caller was a type-loosening with no runtime effect. The narrowing compiles on the head: `Type Check · workspace` and `TypeScript Type Check` are `success`.
7. **The two updated `[#20599]` pins keep their subject — right.** `week-key-year-below-100.test.ts` still pins that a day in 0001..0099 lands in its own ISO week and never the 1900s one (`0050-01-01` → `0049-W52`; 20:00 UTC on the Sunday `0050-01-02` → `0049-W52` in UTC and `0050-W01` in Asia/Shanghai, where it is already Monday); only the key's spelling moves from the Monday's date to the label, and the Monday stays in a comment. Re-spelled, not weakened.
8. **The new pin file is the right shape — right.** `bucket-key-readers-four-digit-year.test.ts` spells the writer's reference keys literally for 0050-06-15, 0050-01-01 (whose week rolls to `0049-W52`), 0999 and a 2026 control; pins `formatDateBucket` as-written for every key at every granularity and the raw-value relabels; pins `bucketDate` equal to the writer for ISO text, epoch ms and a `Date`, and in Asia/Shanghai; and pins both `queryDataset` legs (published: the ObjectQL strategy over `applyInMemoryAggregation` then labels; preview: `previewDrafts`) answering the same rows at all five granularities. The red-first commit `748c4bd5b9` is an ancestor of the head (the branch is two commits: the red pin, then the fix). `@objectstack/objectql` is a declared devDependency of the package, so the test's import is a declared read.
9. **File surface and scope — right.** Five files, all on the claim `5921235126`: the two readers, their pins under `src/__tests__/`, `.changeset/20867-analytics-year-keys.md`. None of the held files (`analytics-service.ts`, the strategies, the normalizer, `read-scope-sql.ts`, `field-read-admission.ts`, `plugin.ts`); no path under `packages/core`, `packages/spec` or `packages/objectql`; no governed surface; the head repo is the base repo; +236 / −64. PR line 1 is `Fixes #20867`, line 2 is `Clause-②: no`.

Nothing in the diff is judged wrong.

### ② Semver level

- The package publishes, so a changeset is owed and one is present: `@objectstack/service-analytics` `patch`; no `skip-changeset` label. `Check Changeset` is `success` on the head.
- Widening: none. No door accepts a value it refused; no export is added.
- Narrowing: none. No input any door admitted is refused now; no export is removed or retyped on the entry (①.1, ①.6).
- The one judgment the ACCEPT left to this review — the preview's `week` key moving from the Monday's date to the ISO label, for every year — is a `patch`, not a `minor` and not a break: the key vocabulary is the published path's declared output contract (`bucketDateKey`'s docblock: an output contract, not a display choice; ADR-0037's continuity of numbers across the publish boundary), the published leg already answered `2026-W25` for the same dataset before this PR, and the preview's Monday spelling was a divergence from that contract that no consumer could depend on without already breaking at publish. The changeset states the change and its consequence (a weekly `compareTo` in the preview now merges onto its week, as published does), so an upgrading reader is told.
- The changeset prose names the four behaviour deltas (four-digit year, ISO week label, epoch-ms bucketed, a `Date` below 1000 keyed by its own year), carries no tracker number and no model identifier, and does not edit any RELEASE-OWNED file.

`Clause-②: no`, no arm — right. Both limbs of the question the line answers (an accept set widened, a public surface expanded) are `no` on the readings above; no `(narrowing)` arm is owed because nothing admitted before is refused now. `no` at `patch` is a consistent pair.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions: []` — none to answer. Every dev flag (os-dev-report `5921673071` `out_of_scope_findings`, PR Acceptance notes, the declared deviation) and the triage direction's open bullet:

- **F1 — a NUMERIC year below 1000 under `year` still labels `1970` (unchanged): answered, agreed as a note, not filed.** No producer answers a numeric year key: the in-memory writer returns a string, and the drivers' bucket expressions (`strftime`, `to_char`, `date_format`, `$dateToString`) answer text; the branch's own comment names the only producer class it exists for (a driver casting `2026` to a number), and a numeric `50` is indistinguishable from 50 epoch-ms by construction. Not escalated.
- **F2 — a raw instant under `week` still labels as its own day key (unchanged): answered, agreed.** A week bucket reaches the labeller as the ISO label on every producer, and that label is now recognised and kept; the raw-value fallback is the `week → YYYY-MM-DD` line the function's header has always documented. Not escalated.
- **F3 — `bucketDate` with a granularity outside the five echoes the raw value: answered, agreed.** Unreachable through the type (`BucketGranularity`), unreachable through the door (①.6), and equal to the engine's in-memory bucketer's own answer (same delegate). Not escalated.
- **F4 — not measured: an HTTP request through `POST /analytics/dataset/query`: answered.** The change sits below the door and touches no request parsing; the `queryDataset`-level readings over both legs are the right altitude for a label and key change; the door's enum was read at schema level (①.6); CI's Test Core and Dogfood lanes exercise the door on the head (verdicts below).
- **F5 — not measured locally: `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:type-check-debt`: answered by CI.** `Type Check · debt ledger` runs `pnpm check:type-check-debt` (lint.yml) — `success`; `Build Core` runs `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` (ci.yml) — `success`.
- **F6 — triage's third bullet, the preview's week vocabulary: answered.** Measured at base (the Monday's date for every year, the 2026 control included), adopted, its consequence stated in the changeset and the PR body, pinned in both test files. Not silently kept.
- **F7 — #20602 (`/export`) stays its own card: agreed**, not on this surface.
- **F8 — the declared deviation (commit trailers carry the repo's model-free trailer pair, not the harness reminder's model-named line): conforming**, read on the head commit; AGENTS.md's rule is the model-free pair, so this is not a deviation from the repo's rule.
- **Independence note:** the dispatching seat and this record share one session id — a dispatched subagent run carries no id of its own. The record was rendered by an isolated contract-review subagent of that seat, which read the card, the PR, the diff and the check-runs and none of the seat's conclusions as input, and is adopted by that seat.
